ArchitecturePerformance
Performance and limits

Cortex separates user-visible response completion from asynchronous memory/graph completion and optional conversation-title work. This avoids coupling response latency to every indexing stage while retaining explicit consistency controls.

Bounded work​

Published policy bounds input/context/output tokens, tool steps, timeout, budgets and concurrency. Retrieval and transcript reads are paginated/bounded. Strict barriers capture finite cutoffs and configured deadlines; a hole or unavailable stage is an explicit result.

Runtime client authentication defaults to 10,000 ms; RPC observation defaults to 12,000 ms, configurable within supported bounds. An issued mutation timeout reports uncertainty rather than cancellation/retry. Retain run/job identities for recovery.

Private upload/delivery is capped at 20,000,000 decoded bytes; providers can impose smaller input limits. Reconnect snapshots retain bounded references rather than copying assets or upstream responses into browser persistence. Asynchronous video generation remains deferred because the official Convex AI Gateway does not support it.

Admission and answer completion​

submitAndStart combines the original initial session check, admission and start request in one parent mutation, followed by an independent fresh session RPC before delivery. The upcoming V6 client uses two admission RPCs while retaining the original authority, approval, queue, identity, generation and expiry checks. Authentication, observation and rendering are additional boundaries. Legacy manual APIs remain available, and a local timeout does not authorize a new intent or a blind execution retry.

Display authorized response text as it arrives. Response completion is independent of later asynchronous facts/chunks/vectors and optional graph work; strict Agents still honor their captured memory barriers before execution. Optional title generation is scheduled after canonical answer finalization and can complete later. Do not include memory readiness or title completion in a first-visible-text measurement.

Fresh ordinary V6 starts atomically claim their run attempt and schedule one owned Action for guarded context preparation, the model step, canonical finalization and background-title enqueue. Strict definitions retain the original Workflow stage barriers and deadlines. A persisted completed first-model tool result attaches an additive Workflow for tools, approval and later model ordinals without replaying ordinal zero. Historical V1–V5 journals are preserved. Duplicate delivery cannot begin another paid operation; interrupted work retains UNKNOWN liability and explicit recovery rather than an automatic model retry. Measure both admission and first-visible-text latency. Agent streaming preserves whole received text fragments and publishes the first nonempty authorized fragment immediately. Later fragments retain bounded batching; every publication still checks current authority, transcript and source witnesses. This upcoming V6 path has source/component checks; hosted latency qualification remains pending.

Context preparation uses bounded, authorized ingestion metadata to route potentially populated context to the existing retrieval path. This avoids repeating the full pending-context and profile probe before full retrieval. Metadata alone never proves that context is empty: the empty path still runs the original pending-context, profile, source, authorization and fresh save checks. A conservative metadata match can route to retrieval even when its full checks later find no indexed context. When the original empty-context proof completes, context saving, model-operation preparation and both policy-resolution checks share a native parent. Populated context uses the original retrieval body, followed by fresh model preparation. The Agent context handler still freshly hydrates before its native pending message write; a prepared-data shortcut failed revocation/write ordering and was rejected. Measure empty and populated memory separately on the installed cloud backend; source acceptance does not establish a latency improvement.

Backend vector and fact retrieval overlap after the original read checks and validated query embedding. Successful results retain deterministic vector-first source bindings and context; failed reads do not publish or save context. Older adapters and tool wrappers retain their guarded serial path unless they explicitly support staged retrieval. This removes sequential retrieval work without adding a model call or retry.

The private V6 Agent query-embedding preflight composes the original authority, profile, readiness, preparation and policy-resolution checks. Server-derived attempt, request, profile, semantic identity, ordinal and budget bindings govern the billable embedding. The original readiness profile child query remains. Admission and the nested dispatch checkpoint share a parent that preserves the reservation if the checkpoint refuses, while rolling back the checkpoint's partial writes. Charge-only capture and private attachment remain separate durable boundaries. Generic public recall and ingestion retain their original preflight; both paths use the unchanged validated-embedding retrieval and final-delivery tail. These are source changes awaiting hosted measurement.

Private observation combines its initial session and authorized output read in one backend mutation, followed by a separate fresh session check before delivery. The canonical demo uses its existing final-authorization observer for run and memory status alongside the text transport, avoiding a separate duplicate status observer. Normal acquisition uses two RPCs; cursor resets and page draining can require further acquisitions. Current principal, scope, protected-source expiry and authentication generation still fence every delivered payload.

Agent model preparation composes the original execution/operation handlers and both policy-resolution checks. Their results propose pinned model inputs; current authorization, qualification, source, transcript and budget controls still run at each billable admission/checkpoint. The outer pre-admission hydration, request binding, admission, parent binding and dispatch checkpoint share one transaction. These changes reduce database handoffs while retaining the current policy, source, lease and budget checks. Their installed latency must be measured separately from source acceptance.

Selected native queries and mutations reuse raw principal, membership, grant, scope and tombstone records within one atomic invocation. Every authorization predicate still runs, returned records are detached, and database or child-mutation writes invalidate the retained reads. The next invocation reads current records again. Source retrieval, final memory delivery and private output observation retain their original read paths. This scope does not retain permissions, model decisions or authority across a network call or process lifetime.

Empty-context preparation can also reuse raw deployment-policy and qualification rows within its own transaction. It fetches that metadata again before saving context, and every original policy, qualification and profile check still runs. This reuse does not cross transactions or replace source and delivery checks.

Selected model-preparation parents also reuse exact raw official Agent message-ID lookups within one invocation. Canonical transcript, current source and authorization checks still run; writes invalidate retained results, and fresh save fences clear them. The installed hosted candidate passed functional qualification, but this does not establish a subsecond response or a controlled speed improvement.

Fresh installations store compact versioned references to the trusted compiled manifest. New accounts inherit the validated installed root. Existing full records remain supported without rewriting their data or financial history. The runtime still reads and validates current controls. Final memory delivery also shares profile and run-budget initialization for vectors with identical complete profiles and budget identities within one transaction; each vector retains its own authorization, source, chunk, receipt, hash and expiry checks. These changes require hosted measurements before reporting latency improvements.

Latency diagnostics​

Diagnostics are opt-in and contain fixed scalar metadata rather than prompts, output, credentials or raw errors. Enable each flag in the process that owns its clock:

Surface	Enablement	Observable boundary
SDK	onLatencyEvent client option	Auth begin/ready/denied, per-RPC begin/end/failed with method/duration, and watcher wake.
Backend	CORTEX_RUNTIME_LATENCY_TRACE=1	Native claim, context retrieval, model-policy, Gateway acquisition/processed-part/text and finalization phase metadata.
Basic CLI	CORTEX_RUNTIME_LATENCY_TRACE=1 in the CLI process	SDK events plus submit begin and first non-whitespace answer write acknowledged by stdout.
Vercel quickstart	NEXT_PUBLIC_CORTEX_LATENCY_TRACE=1 in the app environment	SDK events plus submission, admission delivery, first-text DOM commit, after-paint marker, response-status DOM commit, canonical-answer completion DOM commit and transport completion.

The SDK's RuntimeLatencyEvent includes version, phase, atMs and optional rpcId/method/durationMs. Pair events within the same client clock. Backend timestamps and browser/CLI clocks have different origins; do not subtract their absolute timestamps to invent an end-to-end duration. RPC settlement may occur after a local deadline, and a watcher wake does not imply that text was painted.

Workflow's deterministic handlers disable process, so tracing safely defaults off inside those handlers. Use the actual Workflow journal's step start/completion metadata for memory barriers, context preparation, model steps and title enqueue. Native mutations also keep Date.now() fixed within one transaction; a zero timestamp difference there does not prove zero execution time. Opt-in native mutation spans use performance.now() to measure admission submission, start, final read, run claim and Workflow startup. Match their native execution/request identities; the submission span uses a fixed correlation label because the run does not yet exist. Inclusive start contains claim and Workflow startup, so do not add those nested durations again. Missing or invalid durations remain unavailable.

Hosted Convex is the primary latency measurement environment. Run the canonical clients against a verified disposable cloud database and label the conditions. Docker can host those clients while the backend remains hosted; a local Convex benchmark is separate evidence.

The quickstart records first-text DOM commit from React's layout phase and schedules its after-paint marker with two animation frames, retaining document visibility metadata. The quickstart separately records response.status.dom-commit, transport.complete and answer.complete.dom-commit; canonical answer completion waits for the matching transported assistant message to be committed. Distinguish those markers from the first durable backend part and the first processed native stream text. The CLI's stdout acknowledgement is a separate boundary from a browser paint. Measure submission-to-visible text in the actual foreground application and report the selected boundary explicitly.

The official Gateway provider internally acquires its service token and makes its HTTP request without exposing those subphase hooks. Native stream acquisition combines that opaque work. Processed-part/text markers are not raw network-first-byte measurements and do not reveal OpenAI internal queue timing.

A submission-to-first-visible-text duration below one second is a product target, not a measured result or service guarantee. The October 13 disposable hosted tests of the unreleased 0.39 candidates measured the following actual canonical-client boundaries. The latest candidate reuses raw reads in additional output endpoints and measures native admission subphases; all four of its measured samples still fail the target.

Candidate	Client and condition	First turn	Warm turn	Below one second
Parallel retrieval and policy reads	Vercel quickstart, foreground after paint	7.84 seconds	8.93 seconds	No
Parallel retrieval and policy reads	Basic CLI, first stdout acknowledgement	12.84 seconds	15.01 seconds	No
V5 ordinary-turn consolidation	Vercel quickstart, foreground after paint	7.50 seconds	6.98 seconds	No
V5 ordinary-turn consolidation	Basic CLI, first stdout acknowledgement	12.84 seconds	14.65 seconds	No
Scoped raw transcript reads	Vercel quickstart, foreground after paint	Unavailable	5.20 seconds	Warm: no; first: unavailable
Scoped raw transcript reads	Basic CLI, first stdout acknowledgement	11.37 seconds	14.70 seconds	No
Reduced progress writes and batched source witnesses	Vercel quickstart, foreground after paint	6.80 seconds	6.15 seconds	No
Reduced progress writes and batched source witnesses	Basic CLI, first stdout acknowledgement	10.53 seconds	14.39 seconds	No
Additional output read scopes and admission timings	Vercel quickstart, foreground after paint	5.91 seconds	4.71 seconds	No
Additional output read scopes and admission timings	Basic CLI, first stdout acknowledgement	10.43 seconds	9.92 seconds	No

The latest candidate has zero passes and four measured failures against the 1,000 ms target. Both clients had diagnostics enabled before submission. The preceding scoped-transcript candidate has zero passes, three measured failures and one unavailable timing. Its first browser turn had incorrect diagnostic enablement in its launcher process; that historical timing gap remains unavailable and was not repaired with another inference request.

In each environment, both clients returned their exact requested replies; native verification passed attributed facts, matching vectors, current authorization, complete usage and contiguous indexing through all eight events. The browser was signed out and closed before the CLI samples, and the disposable database and container were verified absent after testing. These are separate empty/populated-context conditions, not a controlled comparison with a historical release. The latency target remains unmet.

The preceding scoped-transcript trace places the first durable text row 4.76/4.21 seconds after run creation for browser first/warm and 8.99/11.09 seconds for CLI first/warm. Those mutation-start timestamps precede durable publication and client display; they are not substitutes for the measured paint or stdout boundary. Processed model-text acquisition took 0.48–0.62 seconds. Cortex orchestration, repeated validation and protected delivery dominate those samples.

In that preceding trace, populated CLI recall took 3.59/4.47 seconds, with query embedding taking only 0.33/0.44 seconds inside those intervals. Facts and vector retrieval overlap, so their child durations must not be added. Native conflict metadata identified background ingestion claims writing event rows during browser preparation and memory-stage persistence writing run rows during visibility checks, causing transaction retries. The progress/source-batch candidate's populated CLI recall took 3.54/5.73 seconds, and total turn preparation took 4.98/7.51 seconds. Reducing those writes and source-query handoffs did not resolve the remaining preparation and delivery cost.

The latest candidate's populated CLI recall took 3.58/4.06 seconds, including only 0.326/0.413 seconds of native embedding. Its recall partitions were 1.056/1.585 seconds before embedding, 0.716/0.575 seconds from result readiness through governed attachment, and 1.486 seconds for the remaining retrieval/source/final-delivery work in each run. Workflow startup itself took 0.935/0.461 seconds in the browser and 0.825/0.591 seconds in the CLI. Answer inference started 3.89/3.06 seconds after committed run creation in the browser and 7.60/7.36 seconds in the CLI, already beyond the target before provider text. These server boundaries are separate from the measured client paint/stdout clocks. Fresh authorization, transcript, source and budget fences remain required. The qualification and timing results do not establish a causal improvement between candidate generations.

The browser's strict readiness check initially returned CONTEXT_INCOMPLETE while asynchronous memory was pending. A later nonbillable check after memory completion confirmed facts and vectors through 4 of 4. This preserves the original failure and demonstrates that response completion and memory readiness are separate states; it is not an inference retry or a repaired latency sample.

The published 0.35 and 0.37 legacy recall implementations have the same four awaited expressions, including parallel vector/fact reads; the newly measured backend runtime is an unreleased 0.39 path. This source comparison does not reconstruct a same-environment historical benchmark or assign an exact version-to-version slowdown.

Measure the right states​

Observe response, memory and graph latency separately. Use current profile metadata, contiguous watermark holes and durable job state to explain waiting. Configure graph only when needed and keep graph credentials in the worker service.

No universal throughput or latency guarantee follows from a source build. Capacity depends on deployment, qualified model bounds, workload and external services. See memory orchestration and model policy.

Distinguish those markers from the first durable backend part and the first processed native stream text. The CLI's stdout acknowledgement is a separate boundary from a browser paint. Measure submission-to-visible text in the actual foreground application and report the selected boundary explicitly.
    - paragraph: The official Gateway provider internally acquires its service token and makes its HTTP request without exposing those subphase hooks. Native stream acquisition combines that opaque work. Processed-part/text markers are not raw network-first-byte measurements and do not reveal OpenAI internal queue timing.
    - paragraph: A submission-to-first-visible-text duration below one second is a product target, not a measured result or service guarantee. The October 13 disposable hosted tests of the unreleased 0.39 candidates measured the following actual canonical-client boundaries. The latest candidate reuses raw reads in additional output endpoints and measures native admission subphases; all four of its measured samples still fail the target.

    - paragraph: The latest candidate has zero passes and four measured failures against the 1,000 ms target. Both clients had diagnostics enabled before submission. The preceding scoped-transcript candidate has zero passes, three measured failures and one unavailable timing. Its first browser turn had incorrect diagnostic enablement in its launcher process; that historical timing gap remains unavailable and was not repaired with another inference request.
    - paragraph: In each environment, both clients returned their exact requested replies; native verification passed attributed facts, matching vectors, current authorization, complete usage and contiguous indexing through all eight events. The browser was signed out and closed before the CLI samples, and the disposable database and container were verified absent after testing. These are separate empty/populated-context conditions, not a controlled comparison with a historical release. The latency target remains unmet.
    - paragraph: The preceding scoped-transcript trace places the first durable text row 4.76/4.21 seconds after run creation for browser first/warm and 8.99/11.09 seconds for CLI first/warm. Those mutation-start timestamps precede durable publication and client display; they are not substitutes for the measured paint or stdout boundary. Processed model-text acquisition took 0.48–0.62 seconds. Cortex orchestration, repeated validation and protected delivery dominate those samples.
    - paragraph: In that preceding trace, populated CLI recall took 3.59/4.47 seconds, with query embedding taking only 0.33/0.44 seconds inside those intervals. Facts and vector retrieval overlap, so their child durations must not be added. Native conflict metadata identified background ingestion claims writing event rows during browser preparation and memory-stage persistence writing run rows during visibility checks, causing transaction retries. The progress/source-batch candidate's populated CLI recall took 3.54/5.73 seconds, and total turn preparation took 4.98/7.51 seconds. Reducing those writes and source-query handoffs did not resolve the remaining preparation and delivery cost.
    - paragraph: The latest candidate's populated CLI recall took 3.58/4.06 seconds, including only 0.326/0.413 seconds of native embedding. Its recall partitions were 1.056/1.585 seconds before embedding, 0.716/0.575 seconds from result readiness through governed attachment, and 1.486 seconds for the remaining retrieval/source/final-delivery work in each run. Workflow startup itself took 0.935/0.461 seconds in the browser and 0.825/0.591 seconds in the CLI. Answer inference started 3.89/3.06 seconds after committed run creation in the browser and 7.60/7.36 seconds in the CLI, already beyond the target before provider text. These server boundaries are separate from the measured client paint/stdout clocks. Fresh authorization, transcript, source and budget fences remain required. The qualification and timing results do not establish a causal improvement between candidate generations.

This preserves the original failure and demonstrates that response completion and memory readiness are separate states; it is not an inference retry or a repaired latency sample.
